newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs end higher, individual stocks lead.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs end higher, individual stocks lead.

text.p: Individual stocks led Wednesday's stock market to a higher close, with cheap and large-cap shares garnering the most attention, brokers said.
The composite index closed trading up 4.54 points to 794.01. Advancing shares beat decliners 601 to 292, while 196 stocks hit their upper trading limit.
But selling pressure at the 800 level proved unsurmountable, and the index retreated from a high of 798.62.
"Economy-related shares and those that were leading the market recently fell sharply," said Kim Sam-soo of Hanil Securities.

Cheap large-cap shares, especially in the Daewoo Group, were also popular on Wednesday. Daewoo Heavy rose 350 won to 6,250 as the most active share of the day. Daewoo Telecom gained 510 won to its upper limit of 9,010, while Daewoo Corp gained 400 won to its limit of 7,070.
Profit-taking hit shares that had risen on foreign investor interest. Sungmi Telecom fell 3,000 won to 190,000, Yukong fell 1,200 won to 21,000, and Samsung Electronics fell 700 won to 66,300.
On Tuesday, the foreign shareholding limit was eased to 20 percent from the previous 18 percent. Foreigners bought selectively, boosting certain blue chips, banks and insurance shares.
The December futures contract closed up 0.35 of a point to 83.50, while the KOSPI 200 index gained 0.42 of a point to 82.72.
